description: A financial services company based in Connecticut, Synchrony has grown into the largest provider of private-label credit cards in the U.S., working with brands including Sam’s Club, Amazon, and Verizon. Synchrony also offers other business lines, including traditional banking savings products and buy-now, pay-later services, which compete against challengers such as Affirm and Klarna. Synchrony can trace its roots back to 1932, initially founded by General Electric to help consumers finance their products. Synchrony spun out from its parent company and went public in 2014, raising nearly $3 billion in its IPO. The company also operates a large network of medical credit cards that offer health care financing through its subsidiary CareCredit.

rankings.itemDescription:
Synchrony's products are designed to help its customers live healthier financial lives, and it’s extending the same mission to its 20,000-plus workers. After 86% of employees voiced they wanted flexibility post-pandemic, the company embraced a hybrid work model, adding the option of attending weekly in-person Connection Days to drive purposeful collaboration. Ask Us Anything town halls, frequent pulse surveys, and leadership roundtables build a cycle of feedback and strengthen employee trust. And the fact that 94% of staffers say Synchrony is a great place to work suggests that it has found perks that actually provide support, including robust childcare benefits, skills-building programs, and diverse wellness offerings. In 2025, Synchrony announced it would invest $1 million over two years to bolster K–12 personal finance education, and launched an employee-led volunteer corps to teach it locally.

"What makes Synchrony a truly great place to work is its genuine emphasis on employee morale and engagement. At Synchrony, we are not viewed simply as employees, but we are recognized as individuals, each with unique motivations and aspirations. Leadership truly understands and encourages us to bring our individual perspectives to our roles. When we come together, we embody ONESYNCHRONY, a unified team built from diverse viewpoints. This authentic focus on people and their well-being is what sets Synchrony apart."

rankings.itemDescription: Rising up from No. 20 on the list this year, Synchrony, one of the largest U.S. issuers of store-branded credit cards, has continued to spur efforts in building workplace belonging and making tangible moves forward in diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Synchrony Women’s Leadership Experience program, in particular, has helped female staff at the VP level break the glass ceiling: Almost half of the program’s participants have been promoted since its 2018 inception. The company has partnerships with Moms First, the Executive Leadership Council, and the Latinx Executive Alliance, among others.  The company plans to invest $50 million in a five-year Education as an Equalizer initiative, with $20 million of the sum to be invested in grants for educational and skills-building opportunities for low-income and underrepresented students and individuals.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Synchrony, one of the largest issuers of store-branded credit cards in the U.S., jumped five spots on the Best Companies to Work For list this year.

  • Synchrony recently revamped its performance evaluation process, scrapping ratings altogether and substituting a single review in favor of three formal conversations throughout the year, although managers are encouraged to hold them more often.

  • Twenty-one of Synchrony’s 24 leadership development programs are available to anyone at the company regardless of their level.

  • The tuition reimbursement program pays up to $24,000 per year in tuition costs and academic fees for full-time employees.

  • In 2022, Synchrony launched its new sabbatical and employee balance programs. The former allows employees to take from one month to a year off from work while still receiving a base salary to cover their benefits, while the latter allows them to work only 20 hours a week for an agreed upon time frame also with benefits.

  • In April 2022, Synchrony unveiled the 10,500-square-foot Synchrony Skills Academy in Stamford, Conn., where high school and adult learners can be trained in digital skills.

rankings.itemDescription: The executive team at this financial services firm has done “a superb job of navigating a dynamic environment,” raves one employee. While approximately 40% of the company’s 16,500-strong workforce were previously equipped to work from home, Synchrony ramped that up to near 100% within two weeks. The company prevented layoffs by instituting a hiring freeze and announcing a voluntary severance program. Synchrony Summer Camp came together quickly, too, pairing more than 3,600 younger children with older kids as “counselors” in a virtual camp setting where over 600 activities including yoga, science experiments, and sign language were on the menu. The stock, which had plummeted to near $12 at the depths of the pandemic, has since rebounded to $42.
